chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught this supplication: 'O Provider of the scarce, O Merciful to the needy, O Guardian of the believers, O Possessor of firm strength. Send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family, and provide for me, grant me well-being, and suffice me for what worries me.'

key_terms.ارْزُقْنِي: Provide for me / Grant me sustenance
key_terms.الْمُقِلِّينَ: The scarce, those with limited means

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication taught by the Prophet for seeking sustenance and relief from worry?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Prophet’s role as a teacher of spiritual remedies, addressing the human condition of need (muqlin) and poverty (masakin). It emphasizes divine attributes of provision and mercy, linking material sustenance with spiritual sufficiency (kafani) to alleviate worldly anxiety, a theme central to Shia devotional practice.
